# `allocation-size-overflow`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports unchecked runtime multiplication used as an allocation length.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Overflow can allocate less memory than the caller expects, making subsequent
indexed writes unsafe.

## When it fires

It applies to recognized allocation calls whose size argument directly contains
runtime multiplication or the addition of two runtime values. A sum of lengths
and literals (`left.len + right.len`) is not reported: lengths of objects in
memory cannot add up past `usize`. Allocations in `test` blocks and in private
functions only tests reach are not reported either, since tests size them from
their own fixed inputs.

The risk is target- and range-dependent: a product that fits `usize` on a
64-bit target may overflow on a narrower supported target, so narrow factors
widened to `usize` count as safe when their declared widths fit 32 bits. When
every factor is widened directly (`@as(usize, width) * @as(usize, height)` with
`u32` dimensions), the widening states the product's intended width and widths
up to 64 bits are accepted. When project invariants establish tighter bounds
than the types express, use a focused suppression rather than changing the
portable arithmetic check.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn grid(allocator: std.mem.Allocator, w: usize, h: usize) ![]u8 {
    return allocator.alloc(u8, w * h);
}
```
